title: Quantile-based SLOs and regional degradation policy for chat endpoints
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define and implement quantile-based SLOs (p50/p95/p99) for conversational/chat endpoints and a regional degradation policy that triggers progressive mitigation (soft throttling, model substitution, regional failover) driven by error-budget burn and sustained tail-latency regressions. This ticket covers spec, metric instrumentation, enforcement primitives (circuit-breaker & shedding controllers), dashboards, and rollout plan.
background: Incidents in Q4 showed that aggregate latency SLOs mask tail events that impact interactive chat UX. We also observed uneven error-budget burn across regions: eu-west-1 had short, high-burn spikes that took longer to recover due to cold start/backfill delays. Existing per-endpoint SLOs are single-metric (p95 latency) with coarse enforcement; we need quantile-aware SLOs and graduated, region-aware mitigation to preserve global availability while minimizing user-visible regressions.
proposal: 1) Define per-endpoint SLI set: token-response latency (p50/p95/p99), request success rate (5xx+model-runtime-errors), and completeness (truncation & early-stops). 2) SLOs: p50=100ms, p95=275ms, p99=600ms (token-response) for chat-fast endpoints; success rate SLO=99.90% per region. 3) Error budget policy: compute burn rate over rolling 6h and 24h windows; define enforcement bands (green/yellow/orange/red) with corresponding actions. 4) Enforcement primitives: a) circuit-breaker that trips on sustained orange/red for >15min, b) shedding controller that applies prefix-based shedding and concurrency limiting, c) model-substitution policy to fallback to smaller quantized variant with lower compute and slightly reduced quality. 5) Routing: when regional health degrades, route X% of traffic to healthy regions incrementally (10/30/60) before full failover. 6) Observability: new dashboard panels and SLO alert rules; synthetic canaries for representative chat prompts to detect semantic regression after model-substitution.
acceptance_criteria: Per-endpoint SLOs published in Confluence and linked in the Console SLO registry
Instrumentation: token-level latency histograms (exposed as t-digest), request success counters, and truncation/failure counters emitted from runtime
Circuit-breaker and shedding controllers implemented as runtime-actuated policies behind feature-flag 'quantile-slo-enforce'
Automated regional routing adjustments implemented in smart-router with configurable steps (10/30/60)
Dashboards: p50/p95/p99 panels, regional burn-rate heatmap, and synthetic canary results visible in Console (runtime-2.3 dashboard)

E2E test: simulate sustained p99 latency spike in eu-west-1 and observe progressive mitigation: shedding -> model-substitution -> incremental routing -> full failover, with alerts and runbook executed
Runbook and on-call playbook updated with error-budget enforcement steps and escalation matrix
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spec+metrics): finalize SLI definitions, add t-digest latency buckets and truncation flags (2 weeks). Phase 2 (controllers): implement circuit-breaker and shedding controller at runtime with feature flag and unit tests (3 weeks). Phase 3 (routing & substitution): wire smart-router hooks for incremental traffic shifting and implement model-substitution strategy (2 weeks). Phase 4 (dashboards & tests): build dashboards and synthetic canaries, run chaos tests in staging (1 week). Rollout: canary enable 5% traffic -> monitor 72h -> 25% -> 100%.
test_plan: - Unit tests for new metrics and controller logic. - Integration tests in staging: inject latency/errors via staging-chaos harness (PR #1423). - Canary: run against canary cluster with representative traffic for 72h. - Load test: spike generation 2x baseline for 1h to validate shedding thresholds and circuit-breaker behavior. - Postmortem criteria: if model-substitution causes >0.5% increase in truncation or user-facing degrade in canary, rollback.
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start 'quantile-slo-enforce' in staging, then prod canary (5% of traffic routed through enforcement). Monitor SLO burn-rate dashboards and synthetic canaries. If burn persists or false positives occur, toggle off. After 7 days of stable metrics, expand to 25% and then full. Coordinate with Dedicated/Private teams to ensure the same logic is available in non-hosted deployments (document SDK hooks).
observability_and_dashboards: New panels to add: token-latency histogram (t-digest), quantile trendlines (p50/p95/p99) per endpoint and per-region, error-budget burn rate (6h/24h), regional availability map, model-substitution impact metrics (quality delta+truncation), and synthetic canary pass rate. Alerts: SLO Yellow (burn_rate>1.5 for 6h) notify #severe-slo; SLO Orange (burn_rate>3 for 1h) page oncall; circuit-breaker trip page with runbook link.
runbook_and_escalation: Runbook steps: 1) Confirm SLO burn (check dashboards & logs). 2) If yellow: throttling adjustments and notify infra. 3) If orange: enable shedding & model-substitution for affected region, notify platform lead and oncall. 4) If red or sustained 2h: shift traffic incrementally to healthy region(s). 5) If immediate degradation: emergency full failover and paged incident. Escalation: oncall -> SRE lead -> Platform Eng -> Product Org call if customer-impacting.
notes_and_decisions: 2026-02-24: Decided to use t-digest histograms rather than fixed buckets to minimize storage overhead while retaining quantile accuracy (Aisha, Marco, Jens)

2026-03-01: Agreed enforcement bands and actions: green (<=1 burn), yellow (1-2 burn): soft throttling, orange (2-4): shedding+model-substitution, red (>4): regional failover (Platform SRE) (Decision by Reliability WG)
2026-03-05: Chose incremental routing steps (10/30/60) to avoid cascading overload in target regions; documented circuit-breaker cooldown of 15m with exponential backoff for reconnect attempts
2026-03-09: Security review deferred; controllers will not expose new external admin APIs and will respect existing RBAC (noted by security team)
